t: A reverse-construction generator and the gate behind 1,100 arrow-puzzle levels
d: All 1,100 Arrow Knots levels come from a reverse-construction generator and pass the G2 pack gate. Fixing the move rule first made each board solvable as built.

t: Daily users rose after the redesign while organic D1 retention fell from 15.2% to 11.2%
d: After an August 2025 redesign, D1 retention of our spelling app's organic cohorts fell from 15.2% to 11.2%; 70% of lost daily users were 31-365 days old.

t: "6.7" < "6.11" is false: comparing Remote Config versions as strings froze content updates
d: A Korean spelling app compared Remote Config content versions as Kotlin strings, so from 6.10 on, devices stored at 6.2 to 6.9 got no quiz or notice updates.

t: Several Claude Code sessions, one repo: the file owner table, checked against 13 merges
d: One commit swept 50 files from another Claude session into a release fix. We built an owner table next; 7 of 13 merges still needed hand merging.

t: R8 kept 5 AdMob test IDs in our release build: one listOf().any line and a dex count
d: A real-ID Block Turn build kept 5 Google test ad strings in its dex. A plain || in place of listOf().any took it to 0. We count IDs and never print them.

t: A month of 'temporary error': our subscription details screen never waited for products, and 1 of 16 users started checkout
d: A Play review said the premium plan showed a 'temporary error' for a month. The details screen never waited for products: 1 of 16 users reached checkout.

t: 16 KB page size support: a blue tint that only NDK 27 and 29 produced, and 12 .so files measured again
d: Six .so files rebuilt for Google Play's 16 KB page rule; NDK 27 and 29 tinted photo transitions blue. Rechecked: NDK 25 aligns to 16 KB with one linker flag.

t: Testers said the time was "too long, so it's easy": checking that with a simulation before cutting puzzle par times by 30%
d: Testers said our puzzle game gave too much time. A 158-level simulation set the cut at 30%; a 45% cut left casual players a 1% three-star rate past level 500.

t: Structured data after FAQ rich results ended: what we kept for GEO
d: Google ended FAQ rich results on May 7, 2026 and Naver on July 9. Why our 106 FAQPage pages stay untouched, and the feed, date and app markup we fixed instead.

t: GA4 said 19 installs yesterday and 8 were real: filtering out test phones and Play pre-launch and review devices
d: sdk_gphone64_arm64 and sdk_gphone16k_arm64 in GA4 were Play pre-launch and review devices. How we filter them and our own test phones out of install counts.

t: A shared LLM cache could have frozen a prompt injection: the blind A/B that let us stop sending context
d: A shared LLM cache keyed without the context could serve one injected answer to every user. A blind A/B showed the context added nothing: 96.0% vs 96.6%.

t: Three agent designs, three judges: the market judge alone would have picked the one that crashed on every KakaoTalk file
d: Before coding a document viewer, 3 agent designs competed and 3 judges scored them. A crash on every KakaoTalk file and 23 plan gaps surfaced before code.

t: A launch crash only on Android 7: one java.time call in a shared module and a NewApi lint gate
d: One java.time call crashed two minSdk 24 games on Android 7. Lint: Call requires API level 26, or core library desugaring. A NewApi gate now blocks release.

t: Commits without a Co-Authored-By trailer: the agent made 26 of the 29 we could check
d: We checked 29 commits without a Co-Authored-By trailer against agent session logs: the agent made 26, mostly merges. Commands to count your own repository.

t: AI coding agents and secrets: one rule in chat, logs and token permissions, and the two exceptions a copied masking regex missed
d: Three ways secrets leak around an AI coding agent: a key in a session log, two exceptions a copied masking regex missed, a deploy plan asking for a wider token.

t: We built three photo apps before checking the market: this year's new apps had a median of 1,166 installs
d: We scraped Google Play only after building three photo apps. The 32 compress apps from 2026 had a median of 1,166 installs; 11 apps were logged as on hold.

t: A static site that several AI agent sessions edit: one --check gate before every commit
d: Several AI agent sessions edit this GitHub Pages site; one --check before each commit demands zero rebuild changes and zero gate errors. Four times it stopped.

t: What "100% E2E pass" really meant: deleting seven runners with zero expect() calls
d: Seven runners behind a "100% E2E pass" since Aug 2025 had zero expect() calls; five never called the app. The night we deleted them, a real E2E logged 7 bugs.

t: A year of AI coding in 701 commits: from "complete" to cause and verification
d: 701 commits recounted: after adopting AI, messages grew from 26 to 233 characters, but fixes stating a cause went from 1 of 29 to 56 of 73 only a year later.

t: We built an edit feature and shipped it switched off: the HWP save gate that caught a form-field bug
d: A gate that diffs edited HWP files record by record caught a form-field bug. 1.1.0 shipped with edit behind a flag; 1.3.0 turned it on nine days later.

t: Puzzle game day-one churn: per-device event timelines, exact board math and four walls in chapter one
d: 7 of 16 ad-acquired devices stalled on board 4 of a block puzzle without a solve. Per-device event timelines and exact per-board win rates found four walls.

t: Running an AI marketer on a schedule four times a day: the permission table that leaves money, accounts and policy to a person
d: Our scheduled AI marketing agent reads one permission table every run. An approved ad restart click was still refused by a tool check, so a person clicked it.

t: Privacy policy AI processing location (cross-border transfer): a notice fixed twice in one day, then tied to code
d: A Vertex AI global endpoint cannot be named as one country, so our privacy policy says processing may happen outside Korea, tied to code and CI.

t: Android showed some Hangul as blank gaps: NanumSquare's cmap claimed 11,172 syllables but drew only 2,479
d: An Android app font listed all 11,172 Hangul syllables in its cmap, but 8,693 had no outline, so text vanished with no fallback. Cause, numbers, a check script.

t: 84 agents reviewed a release: three refuters per finding, and only the 20 survivors got fixed
d: SugarSpeller 1.6.025's release review ran 84 agents with three refuters per finding. 20 findings survived, one of them a crash, and the second pass confirmed 0.

t: androidx.pdf beta01 runs your Application.onCreate a second time, in an isolated process, and the PDF silently never opens
d: androidx.pdf beta01 parses PDFs in an isolated process that also runs your Application.onCreate. Without a guard, the PDF never opened and no error came back.

t: Our contrast checker passed while skipping 40% of the text: make it print how much it measured
d: A contrast check that passed in three themes had silently dropped 3,762 of 9,318 text fragments (40%). Now it prints what it measured and fails on a shortfall.

t: Jetpack Compose splits Korean between syllables, but the stacked 'R/u/l/e' label came from how a Row measures
d: Compose can break Korean between syllables, but the label stacked as 'R/u/l/e' on a Galaxy S21 came from Row measurement order. Each cause got its own fix.

t: "Use hundreds of agents" in practice: 10 workstreams, 59 commits in a day, three running at once
d: The operator allowed hundreds of agents, but only three code-writing agents ran at once. 4 GB of free RAM and two shared phones set the pace of a 59-commit day.

t: A 20% staged rollout went out at 100%: a completed release in the Play Publisher API cannot go back to staged
d: SugarSpeller 1.6.029 was meant for 20% via the Play Publisher API but was committed as completed; Play refused the move back to 20% with a 403. Cause and guard.

t: 3,066 green tests hid a line that breaks opening the database: checking tests by deleting the guard
d: A P2P chat app passed 3,066 tests while one SQLite pragma, traced through plugin source, kept its database from opening. Now we judge tests by deleting guards.

t: Play Console said our DEX was 39% optimized. The culprit was a keep rule for an SDK we never used
d: Removing -dontoptimize left Play Console's DEX metrics at 36-39%. Deleting an unused Kakao SDK keep rule took r8.json to 85% and the AAB to 11.6 MB.

t: Every sitemap lastmod had the same date: deriving modified dates from a content hash
d: All 51 sitemap URLs once shared one lastmod. Now dates follow a hash of each page's main content, not commit dates, and a 99-file commit moved only 6 of them.

t: Block puzzle difficulty: how simulation bots caught a game you could never lose
d: Our block puzzle spec promised every tray could always be placed. A planning bot then played 80 games; all 80 hit the 3,000-move cap. How two bots set the fix.

t: The agent said it was tested. The game crashed on the first tutorial tap: a missing VIBRATE permission and the fresh-install monkey test
d: Our AI agent called a puzzle game crash-free, then it died on the first tutorial tap: a missing VIBRATE permission. adb monkey on clean data hit it at event 15.

t: Building an Android HWP viewer: rhwp in a WebView, measured on 222 documents
d: The open-source rhwp engine in an Android WebView opened 221 of 222 Korean HWP/HWPX files on a Galaxy S21; a 384-page file needed virtual scrolling.

t: How we shipped four Android apps in 20 days with an AI coding agent
d: A solo developer and Claude Code put four Android apps on Google Play within 20 days of the first commit. 52 of 59 commits were co-authored with the agent.

t: How to write AGENTS.md: only the rules an AI coding agent gets wrong
d: AGENTS.md is the file an AI coding agent reads before it works. Ours has 96 lines, lists only the rules the agent gets wrong, and enforces key ones with tests.

t: What to check before shipping an AI-built Android app: the release gate and an R8 crash
d: Our Android app ran fine in debug but crashed at launch in release after R8 removed a constructor. Now every upload passes three pre-release checks.
